key: must:F30a:The audio lasts 10 seconds, within 0.1 second.
symptom: The audio lasts 10 seconds, within 0.1 second.

whys.why: Why does the delivered audio not last 10 s within 0.1 s?
whys.because: Every chat delivered a single untrimmed generate_music output that is 15 s long, or 30 s in old.stupid. Nothing in the chat cut it to 10 s.
whys.evidence: s2.new.dumper.F30a/grade.json: check 'about 10 s' failed with got '15 s', and the grader wrote 'The file is 15 s. The user agreed to trim it themselves'. s2.old.stupid.F30a/calls.jsonl: duration 30, and the reply says 'a 30-second instrumental lo-fi track'.

whys.why: Why did the assistant request 15 s when the user asked for 10 s?
whys.because: The generate_music schema rejects anything shorter than 15 s, so 15 is the closest value it can send.
whys.evidence: tools-new.json, generate_music: "duration": {"minimum": 15, "maximum": 300, "description": "Requested track duration in seconds, from 15 to 300"}. new.happy and old.dumper calls.jsonl both send duration 15. The old.stupid reply repeats 'from 15 seconds to 5 minutes', so the old build has the same limit.

whys.why: Why did the assistant not cut the 15 s track to 10 s after generation?
whys.because: Neither build has a tool that trims an audio file. The only edit tools work on video (join_videos, edit_video and others), and generate_music has no trim option. So the assistant told the user to trim the file themselves.
whys.evidence: tools-new.json: no audio trim tool is defined (trim_video appears only in plan_request's enum, and join_videos takes 'videos'). new.happy calls.jsonl reply: 'The music generator can't make anything shorter than 15 seconds. I can't cut audio here, so trim it to 10 seconds in any audio or video editor.' old.dumper reply: 'You cut it down to 10 seconds in any audio or video editor.'

whys.why: Why did the new build's planning step not catch or route around the length conflict?
whys.because: plan_request returned ready:true with seconds=10 for generate_music. It did not warn about the 15 s minimum or offer a way to post-process. Even a warning could not have produced a 10 s file, because no trim step exists.
whys.evidence: s2.new.happy.F30a/calls.jsonl, plan_request output: {"tool":"generate_music","ready":true,"params":[...{"name":"seconds","value":10}],"questions":[]}. The next call is generate_music with duration 15.

whys.why: Why did old.stupid get 30 s instead of 15 s?
whys.because: This is a secondary cause that applies only to this persona. The stupid user said only 'make me some background music' and never gave a length. The old build has no plan_request to flag the missing value, so the assistant picked 30 s itself. A 10 s result was impossible anyway because of the 15 s floor.
whys.evidence: s2.old.stupid.F30a/state.json: the user's only message is 'make me some background music'. calls.jsonl: generate_music duration 30, with no question asked first.

result.axiom: The Magic Hour music generator cannot make a track shorter than 15 s (duration minimum 15). Neither MCP build has a tool that trims audio, so a 10 s music file cannot be delivered.
result.fix: Add a server-side audio trim step to the new build, using the same ffmpeg path that join_videos uses. Two options: (a) add a trim_audio(audio, start_seconds, end_seconds) tool, or (b) let generate_music accept any duration below 15 s by generating 15 s and returning a copy cut to the requested length with a short fade-out. In both cases, plan_request should report that generate_music under 15 s needs this trim step and route to it.
